(p-516) Surah al-Mumtahanah

Medinan, according to all.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies﴾. The occasion of its revelation: when the Prophet ﷺ intended to set out toward Makkah, he gave the impression that he intended Khaybar. Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah wrote to the people of Makkah that the Prophet ﷺ was coming out against them, and he sent it with a woman, who was mentioned (p-517) to be named Sarah, a freedwoman of the Banu Abd al-Muttalib. The Prophet ﷺ was informed of this, so he dispatched Ali and Abu Marthad. It was said that it was Umar ibn al-Khattab, and it was said that it was al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them. He said to them: "Go to Rawdat Khakh, for you will meet a woman there carrying a letter; take it from her and return." They went to the place and found her, and the letter was with her. They took it and returned. When it was examined, it was the letter of Hatib. Umar said: "Permit me, O Messenger of Allah, to strike his neck, for he has betrayed Allah and His Messenger." The Prophet ﷺ said: "He witnessed Badr." They said: "Yes, but he has broken faith and aided your enemies against you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Perhaps Allah has looked upon the people of Badr and said: 'Do what you wish, for I am Aware of what you do.'"

Umar's eyes overflowed, and he said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." [Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Hatib:] "What moved you to do what you did?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I was a man attached to Quraysh, and I had property there, so I wrote to them about this. By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I truly believe in Allah and His Messenger." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Hatib has spoken the truth, so say nothing to him but good."

Then this verse and the one after it were revealed.

» Regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You confide to them with affection﴾, there are two possible meanings:

One: you inform them secretly that there is affection between you and them.

The second: you inform them secretly of the affairs of the Prophet ﷺ, with affection between you and them.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 60, verses 4–6:

﴿Indeed there has been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him﴾. Al-Kalbi and al-Farra' mentioned that it refers to Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. Regarding it there are two interpretations (p-518):
One: an excellent sunnah (practice), said by al-Kalbi.

The second: an excellent lesson, said by Ibn Qutaybah.

﴿in Abraham and those with him﴾, from among the believers.

﴿When they said to their people﴾, meaning from among the disbelievers.

﴿Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah﴾. So they disowned them. Why, then, did you not disown them, O Hatib, from the disbelievers of the people of Makkah, and not do what you did of corresponding with them and informing them?

Then He said ﴿We have rejected you﴾, which may have two meanings:

One: We reject what you have believed in of idols.

The second: We reject your deeds and deny them.

﴿And there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone﴾, except for the statement of Abraham to his father: ﴿I will surely ask forgiveness for you﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

One: Follow Abraham in his conduct and emulate him, except in seeking forgiveness for his father; do not emulate him in that. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: its meaning is "except Abraham," for he excepted his father from his people in seeking forgiveness for him. This was related by al-Kalbi.

﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the disbelievers﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

One: its meaning is, do not give them power over us so that they tempt us. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: do not punish us at their hands, nor with a punishment from You, lest we become a trial for them so that they say, "Had they been upon the truth, they would not have been punished." This was said by Mujahid, and this is from the supplication of Abraham, peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 60, verse 7–9:

﴿It may be that Allah will bring about affection between you and those among them with whom you have been at enmity.﴾ On this there are two opinions:

The first: the people of Makkah, when they embraced Islam in the year of the Conquest (al-Fath), and that is the affection that came to be between them and the Muslims. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

The second: that it refers to the Islam of Abu Sufyan.

Regarding the affection that came from him, there are two opinions:

The first: the marriage of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Umm Habibah, the daughter of Abu Sufyan, and this was an affection between him and Abu Sufyan. This is the view of Muqatil.

The second: the Prophet (ﷺ) appointed Abu Sufyan over some part of Yemen, and when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, he set out and encountered Dhu al-Khimar, who had apostatized, and fought him. He was thus the first to fight in the apostasy (al-Ridda) and to strive (jihad) on behalf of the religion, and this was the affection. This is the view of al-Zuhayri.

﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion﴾, and so on.

On this there are four aspects:

The first: that this was at the beginning of the matter, at the time of the truce (muwada'ah) with the polytheists, and then it was abrogated (nusikha) by fighting. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

The second: that they were Khuza'ah and the Banu al-Harith ibn Abd Manaf, who had a covenant, so Allah commanded that they be treated with kindness and fulfilment of the covenant. This is the view of Muqatil.

The third: that they are the women and the children, because they are among those who do not fight. So Allah permitted kindness toward them. This was related by some of the exegetes.

The fourth: what Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr related from his father: "that Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) divorced his wife Qutaylah in the Jahiliyyah, and she was the mother of Asma' bint Abi Bakr. She came to them during the period in which there was a truce (muhadanah) between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the disbelievers of Quraysh, and she gave Asma' bint Abi Bakr a pair of earrings and other things. Asma' disliked accepting them from her until she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, so Allah revealed this verse."

﴿And that you deal justly with them﴾. Regarding this there are two aspects:

The first: meaning that you act justly toward them. This is the view of Ibn Habban: so do not go to excess in drawing close to them, nor be extravagant in keeping away from them.

The second: its meaning is that you give them a portion of your wealth. This was related by Ibn Isa.

It may also be understood as a third: that it means spending on those among them whose maintenance is obligatory, and difference of religion does not prevent their entitlement to it.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 60, verse 10–11:

﴿O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. Allah is most knowing of their faith.﴾ Because He knows, through the examination, the outward appearance of their faith, whereas Allah knows the inward reality of their faith, so that the ruling concerning them is based on the outward, although it is also based on the outward and the inward.

The occasion of the revelation of this verse is that the Prophet ﷺ made a truce with the Quraysh in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah. The Quraysh said, "On condition that you return to us whoever comes to you from us, and we return to you whoever comes to us from you." He said, "On condition that I return to you whoever comes to us from you, and you return to us whoever comes to you from us, from among those who chose disbelief over faith." (p-521) He then kept the truce between himself and them on this basis, until a Muslim woman came to him from them, and they came seeking her. There are four opinions concerning her:

The first: She is Umaymah bint Bishr, who was married to Thabit ibn al-Dahdahah. She fled from him while he was at that time a disbeliever, and Sahl ibn Hunayf married her, and she bore him ʿAbd Allah. This was said by Yazid ibn Abi Habib.

The second: She is Saʿidah, the wife of Safwan ibn al-Rahib, a polytheist from the people of Makkah. This was said by Muqatil.

The third: She is Umm Kulthum bint ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt. This is the view of many people of knowledge.

The fourth: She is Subayʿah bint al-Harith al-Aslamiyyah, who came as a Muslim after the Prophet ﷺ had finished writing the truce at al-Hudaybiyyah. Her husband, whose name was Musafir, and who was from her people, came seeking her, and said, "O Muhammad, you stipulated for us the return of women, and the ink of the document has not dried yet. This is my wife, so return her to me." This was related by al-Kalbi.

When the polytheists demanded the return of the women who had embraced Islam, Allah forbade their return after examining their faith, by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿If you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers.﴾ The people of knowledge differed as to whether the women were included in the terms of the truce, either explicitly or by general implication. One group said: the condition of their return was explicitly stated in the truce, so Allah abrogated their return from the agreement and prohibited it, while leaving it in place for the men as it was. This indicates that the Prophet ﷺ may exercise his own judgment in rulings, but Allah the Exalted does not let him persist in an error.

Another group of the people of knowledge said: he did not stipulate their return explicitly in the agreement; rather, the agreement was stated generally regarding the return of those who embraced Islam. The apparent generality included them along with the men, so Allah clarified their exclusion from the generality and distinguished them from the men for two reasons:

The first: they are women with private parts that are forbidden to the men.

The second: they are softer of heart and quicker to change than the men.

As for the one who remained upon her polytheism, she is returned to them. Some of them, when they wished to harm their husbands, would say, "I will emigrate to Muhammad," and therefore the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to examine them.

There are three opinions concerning what he examined them with:

The first: what Ibn ʿAbbas narrated, that he would examine her by having her swear by Allah that she had not left out of hatred for her husband, nor out of desire to move from land to land, nor seeking worldly gain, nor out of love for a man among us, and that she had only left out of love for Allah and His Messenger.

The second: that she bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. This was said by ʿAtiyyah al-ʿAwfi.

The third: what Allah clarified in the surah by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you﴾. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿examine them. Allah is most knowing of their faith﴾, meaning, of what is in their hearts after their examination.

﴿If you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them⁠—﴾ meaning that the believing women are forbidden to the polytheists among the idol-worshippers, and the apostate women are forbidden to the Muslims.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And give them what they have spent﴾, meaning, the bridal gifts of those among them who embraced Islam, if their husbands asked for that. Concerning the giving of this to their families rather than to their husbands, there are two opinions. Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And there is no blame upon you in marrying them﴾, meaning the believing women who embraced Islam while not married to polytheist husbands. Allah permitted their marriage to the Muslims once their waiting period had ended, or if they had not been consummated with.

﴿When you have given them their compensation﴾, meaning their bridal gifts.

﴿And do not hold on to marriage with disbelieving women﴾. On this there are two meanings:

The first: that ʿiṣmah means beauty; this was said by Ibn Qutaybah.

The second: that it means the marriage contract; this was said by al-Kalbi.

So when a disbeliever from among the idolaters embraces Islam, he may not keep his marriage to her or maintain it out of desire for her or her people. Allah has forbidden his marrying her and remaining with her as long as she has not embraced Islam within her waiting period.

Musa ibn Talhah ibn ʿUbayd Allah related from his father that he said: When this verse was revealed, Arwa bint Rabiʿah ibn al-Harith ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib (p-523) was divorced, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab divorced Qurayba bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, and after him Muʿawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married her while she was still a polytheist. And he divorced Umm Kulthum bint Abi Jarwal al-Khuzaʿiyyah, mother of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, and after him Khalid ibn Saʿid ibn al-ʿAs married her in Islam.

﴿And ask for what you have spent, and let them ask for what they have spent﴾, meaning that if a Muslim's wife apostatizes to the polytheists from among the people of the aforementioned covenant, he may recover from them the bridal gift of his wife as we have mentioned; and that the polytheist may recover the bridal gift of his wife when she embraces Islam. If there was no covenant between us and them stipulating return, then he may not recover it.

It is not permissible for any imam after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to stipulate in a truce agreement the return of those who embrace Islam, because the Messenger was under a promise from Allah of the conquest of their lands and their entry into Islam, willingly or unwillingly, so what was lawful for him was not lawful for others.

﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers﴾ to the end of the verse.

The meaning is that whoever's wife has been lost to him by her apostasy to the people of the aforementioned covenant, and he has not received her bridal gift from them, and then the Muslims take booty from them, they shall return her bridal gift to him.

Concerning the property from which this bridal gift is returned, there are three opinions:

The first: from the spoils of their booty, because it is owed to them by right; this was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: from the fay' property; this was said by al-Zuhri.

The third: from the dowry of those women among them who embraced Islam while married to a disbelieving husband; this is also narrated from al-Zuhri.

Concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿then you take booty﴾ (fa-ʿaqabtum), there are three interpretations:

The first: its meaning is "you gained booty," by taking it from the raid (muʿaqabat al-ghazw); this was said by Mujahid and al-Dahhak.

The second: its meaning is "you obtained from the outcome (ʿaqibah) of those who were killed or taken captive"; this was said by Sufyan.

The third: "you punished (ʿaqabtum) the apostate woman by killing her, so her husband's bridal gift is from the spoils of the Muslims"; this was said by Ibn Bahr.

This ruling is abrogated, due to the abrogation of the condition which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stipulated for them at al-Hudaybiyyah. ʿAta' said, rather its ruling remains in force.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 60, verse 10–11:

﴿O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. Allah is most knowing of their faith.﴾ Because He knows, through the examination, the outward appearance of their faith, whereas Allah knows the inward reality of their faith, so that the ruling concerning them is based on the outward, although it is also based on the outward and the inward.

The occasion of the revelation of this verse is that the Prophet ﷺ made a truce with the Quraysh in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah. The Quraysh said, "On condition that you return to us whoever comes to you from us, and we return to you whoever comes to us from you." He said, "On condition that I return to you whoever comes to us from you, and you return to us whoever comes to you from us, from among those who chose disbelief over faith." (p-521) He then kept the truce between himself and them on this basis, until a Muslim woman came to him from them, and they came seeking her. There are four opinions concerning her:

The first: She is Umaymah bint Bishr, who was married to Thabit ibn al-Dahdahah. She fled from him while he was at that time a disbeliever, and Sahl ibn Hunayf married her, and she bore him ʿAbd Allah. This was said by Yazid ibn Abi Habib.

The second: She is Saʿidah, the wife of Safwan ibn al-Rahib, a polytheist from the people of Makkah. This was said by Muqatil.

The third: She is Umm Kulthum bint ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt. This is the view of many people of knowledge.

The fourth: She is Subayʿah bint al-Harith al-Aslamiyyah, who came as a Muslim after the Prophet ﷺ had finished writing the truce at al-Hudaybiyyah. Her husband, whose name was Musafir, and who was from her people, came seeking her, and said, "O Muhammad, you stipulated for us the return of women, and the ink of the document has not dried yet. This is my wife, so return her to me." This was related by al-Kalbi.

When the polytheists demanded the return of the women who had embraced Islam, Allah forbade their return after examining their faith, by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿If you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers.﴾ The people of knowledge differed as to whether the women were included in the terms of the truce, either explicitly or by general implication. One group said: the condition of their return was explicitly stated in the truce, so Allah abrogated their return from the agreement and prohibited it, while leaving it in place for the men as it was. This indicates that the Prophet ﷺ may exercise his own judgment in rulings, but Allah the Exalted does not let him persist in an error.

Another group of the people of knowledge said: he did not stipulate their return explicitly in the agreement; rather, the agreement was stated generally regarding the return of those who embraced Islam. The apparent generality included them along with the men, so Allah clarified their exclusion from the generality and distinguished them from the men for two reasons:

The first: they are women with private parts that are forbidden to the men.

The second: they are softer of heart and quicker to change than the men.

As for the one who remained upon her polytheism, she is returned to them. Some of them, when they wished to harm their husbands, would say, "I will emigrate to Muhammad," and therefore the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to examine them.

There are three opinions concerning what he examined them with:

The first: what Ibn ʿAbbas narrated, that he would examine her by having her swear by Allah that she had not left out of hatred for her husband, nor out of desire to move from land to land, nor seeking worldly gain, nor out of love for a man among us, and that she had only left out of love for Allah and His Messenger.

The second: that she bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. This was said by ʿAtiyyah al-ʿAwfi.

The third: what Allah clarified in the surah by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O Prophet, when believing women come to you﴾. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿examine them. Allah is most knowing of their faith﴾, meaning, of what is in their hearts after their examination.

﴿If you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them⁠—﴾ meaning that the believing women are forbidden to the polytheists among the idol-worshippers, and the apostate women are forbidden to the Muslims.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And give them what they have spent﴾, meaning, the bridal gifts of those among them who embraced Islam, if their husbands asked for that. Concerning the giving of this to their families rather than to their husbands, there are two opinions. Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And there is no blame upon you in marrying them﴾, meaning the believing women who embraced Islam while not married to polytheist husbands. Allah permitted their marriage to the Muslims once their waiting period had ended, or if they had not been consummated with.

﴿When you have given them their compensation﴾, meaning their bridal gifts.

﴿And do not hold on to marriage with disbelieving women﴾. On this there are two meanings:

The first: that ʿiṣmah means beauty; this was said by Ibn Qutaybah.

The second: that it means the marriage contract; this was said by al-Kalbi.

So when a disbeliever from among the idolaters embraces Islam, he may not keep his marriage to her or maintain it out of desire for her or her people. Allah has forbidden his marrying her and remaining with her as long as she has not embraced Islam within her waiting period.

Musa ibn Talhah ibn ʿUbayd Allah related from his father that he said: When this verse was revealed, Arwa bint Rabiʿah ibn al-Harith ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib (p-523) was divorced, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab divorced Qurayba bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, and after him Muʿawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married her while she was still a polytheist. And he divorced Umm Kulthum bint Abi Jarwal al-Khuzaʿiyyah, mother of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, and after him Khalid ibn Saʿid ibn al-ʿAs married her in Islam.

﴿And ask for what you have spent, and let them ask for what they have spent﴾, meaning that if a Muslim's wife apostatizes to the polytheists from among the people of the aforementioned covenant, he may recover from them the bridal gift of his wife as we have mentioned; and that the polytheist may recover the bridal gift of his wife when she embraces Islam. If there was no covenant between us and them stipulating return, then he may not recover it.

It is not permissible for any imam after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to stipulate in a truce agreement the return of those who embrace Islam, because the Messenger was under a promise from Allah of the conquest of their lands and their entry into Islam, willingly or unwillingly, so what was lawful for him was not lawful for others.

﴿And if any of your wives go over to the disbelievers﴾ to the end of the verse.

The meaning is that whoever's wife has been lost to him by her apostasy to the people of the aforementioned covenant, and he has not received her bridal gift from them, and then the Muslims take booty from them, they shall return her bridal gift to him.

Concerning the property from which this bridal gift is returned, there are three opinions:

The first: from the spoils of their booty, because it is owed to them by right; this was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: from the fay' property; this was said by al-Zuhri.

The third: from the dowry of those women among them who embraced Islam while married to a disbelieving husband; this is also narrated from al-Zuhri.

Concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿then you take booty﴾ (fa-ʿaqabtum), there are three interpretations:

The first: its meaning is "you gained booty," by taking it from the raid (muʿaqabat al-ghazw); this was said by Mujahid and al-Dahhak.

The second: its meaning is "you obtained from the outcome (ʿaqibah) of those who were killed or taken captive"; this was said by Sufyan.

The third: "you punished (ʿaqabtum) the apostate woman by killing her, so her husband's bridal gift is from the spoils of the Muslims"; this was said by Ibn Bahr.

This ruling is abrogated, due to the abrogation of the condition which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stipulated for them at al-Hudaybiyyah. ʿAta' said, rather its ruling remains in force.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 60, verse 12:

﴿O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you, that they will not associate anything with Allah﴾ And that is because when the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah in the year of the Conquest, and the men had pledged allegiance to him, the women came after them to pledge allegiance, and he accepted their pledge.

There is a difference of opinion regarding his pledging allegiance to them, in three statements:

The first: that he sat on al-Safa [with ʿUmar below him], and he commanded him to take the pledge from the women. This was said by Muqatil.

The second: that he commanded Umaymah, the sister of Khadijah and maternal aunt of Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah, after she had pledged allegiance to him, to take the pledge from the women on his behalf. This was said by Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Umaymah.

The third: that he took the pledge from them personally, with a garment placed over his hand. This was said by ʿAmir al-Shaʿbi.

It is also said that rather, he placed a bowl (qaʿb) containing water, dipped his hand in it, and commanded them, and they dipped their hands in it. This was the pledge of the women.

If it is asked: what is the meaning of their pledge, since they are not among the people of jihad, so that the pledge is taken from them as it is from men? It is said: his pledge to them was an instruction to them regarding what was incumbent upon them of the rights of Allah the Exalted and the rights of their husbands, because they had entered into the Sharia and did not know its ruling, so he clarified it for them. The first thing he took from them was that they should not associate anything with Allah, affirming His unity and forbidding the worship of other than Him.

﴿And that they will not steal﴾ It is narrated that Hind bint ʿUtbah was disguised when the pledge was being taken from the women, out of fear of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) because of what she had done to Hamzah and her eating of his liver. When she heard him say in taking the pledge from them, "that they will not steal," she said: "By Allah, I only take from Abu Sufyan what is our sustenance, and I do not know whether that is lawful for me or not." Abu Sufyan said: "What you have taken of the past or what remains, it is lawful for you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed, recognised her, and said: "Are you Hind?" She said: "Allah has pardoned what has passed."

Then he said, ﴿And that they will not commit adultery﴾ Hind said: "O Messenger of Allah, does a free woman commit adultery?"

Then he said, ﴿And that they will not kill their children﴾ because the Arabs used to bury daughters alive. Hind said: "You killed them on the day of Badr, and you and they are the most knowing."

Muqatil narrated that she said: "We raised them as little ones and you killed them as grown ones, so you and they know best." ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab laughed until he fell onto his back.

﴿And that they will not bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾ Regarding this there are three statements:

The first: that it is sorcery, said by Ibn Bahr.

The second: walking about with tale-bearing and striving in corruption.

The third, which is the view of the majority: that they not attribute to their husbands children other than their own, because a wife would pick up a child (foundling) and attribute it to her husband as a child. The meaning of ﴿between their hands﴾ is what she took up as a foundling, and ﴿their feet﴾ is what she bore from fornication. It is narrated that when Hind heard that, she said: "By Allah, slander is a shameful matter, and he only commands what is most right and noble of character."

Then he said, ﴿And that they will not disobey you in what is right﴾ Regarding this there are four interpretations:

The first: that "what is right" here is obedience to Allah and His Messenger. This was said by Maymun ibn Mihran.

The second: what Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated from Umm Salamah, "from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿And that they will not disobey you in what is right﴾, he said: it is wailing."

The third: that among what is right is that they not scratch their faces, nor loosen their hair, nor tear their collars, nor cry out "woe." This was said by Usayd ibn Abi Usayd.

The fourth: that it is general to every right thing that Allah and His Messenger have commanded. This was said by al-Kalbi.

It is narrated that Hind said at that point: "We did not sit in this gathering of ours with any intention of giving you anything." This is evidence that obedience to rulers is only binding in what is permissible and right, not in what is forbidden and prohibited.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 60, verse 13:

﴿O you who have believed, do not take as allies a people with whom Allah is angry﴾. Regarding this, there are three opinions:

The first: they are the Jews. This is the view of Muqatil.

The second: they are the Jews and the Christians. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud.

The third: they are all the disbelievers. This is the view of Mujahid.

﴿They have despaired of the Hereafter, as the disbelievers have despaired of the companions of the graves﴾. Regarding this, there are four interpretations:

The first: they have despaired of the reward of the Hereafter, just as the disbelievers have despaired of the resurrection of those in the graves. This is the view of Ibn Abbas.

The second: they have despaired of the reward of the Hereafter, just as the companions of the graves, after witnessing it, despair of the reward of the Hereafter, because they have become certain of the punishment. This is the view of Mujahid.

The third: they have despaired of the resurrection and the return, just as those among them who died and were buried have despaired of it.

The fourth: they have despaired that there will be any good for them in the Hereafter, just as they have despaired that any good from the companions of the graves will reach them.
